deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. No formulas, equations or derivations appear, so nothing can be reconstructed in modern notation. The page is purely methodological prose. It is page 3 of the introductory part of Riemann's fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres' (published posthumously by J. Henle, Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin, 3. Reihe, Bd. 29, 1867; reprinted in the Gesammelte Werke). The foliation '10' is visible in the right margin.

The previous page described and rejected the 'synthetic way' in the physiology of the sense organs: building up the organ's function from the measured physical properties of its parts. That approach is unreliable for microscopic objects and forces arbitrary appeals to analogy or teleology.

This page introduces the 'analytic way' (Analytischer Weg). One starts from the observed performances (Leistungen) of the organ and seeks their explanation in its structure. In the corrected reading, 'sucht man zu den Leistungen des Organs die Erklärung'. The task has three parts:
(1) Find a hypothesis sufficient to explain the performances ('genügt', underlined).
(2) Examine to what extent that hypothesis is necessary for the explanation ('nothwendig', underlined).
(3) Compare it with experience, to confirm or correct it.

Under I, Riemann says one must 're-invent' the instrument. Insofar, the organ's performances are treated as end and its creation as means. But the end is not conjectured; it is given by experience. If one sets aside how the organ came to be made, the concept of final causes (Endursachen) can stay entirely out of play. One then seeks the explanation of the factual performances in the organ's construction. The page breaks off at 'Bei dem Aufsuchen dieser Erklärung hat man zuvörderst'. The next page continues: first analyse the organ's task into secondary tasks, then infer from the anatomy how they are solved.

In modern terms this is a schema for inverse or functional modelling: posit a sufficient model, test which of its assumptions are necessary (eliminating arbitrary ones), then test it against experiment. It parallels the logical distinction between sufficient and necessary conditions. Nothing has been filled in by me.

results.what: Methodological schema for the physiology of sense organs. Explain the organ from its observed performance by three steps: a sufficient hypothesis, an examination of its necessity, and an empirical check. Teleological language is explicitly confined so that final causes are not needed.
results.modern_name: Analytic/functional (reverse-engineering) method; hypothetico-deductive modelling with sufficiency/necessity analysis
results.usually_credited_to: General 19th-century scientific methodology (cf. Helmholtz, Herbart-influenced epistemology); this specific text is Riemann's own, from 'Mechanik des Ohres' (publ. 1867 by Henle)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the methodological introduction of Riemann's 'Mechanik des Ohres'. It was published posthumously in 1867 and is included in his collected works, so it is well known as his. It contains no mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Lines 1-3: the interlinear insertions are corrections, not additions. 'sucht' is written above 'geht' and replaces it; 'zu' is written above 'von' and replaces it; 'die Erklärung' is written above 'aus' and replaces it. The intended reading is 'Bei dem zweiten Wege sucht man zu den Leistungen des Organs die Erklärung.' This matches the published text. In the image the replaced words appear unstruck, but the revision is clear.

In '1, ... zur Erklärung der Leistungen genügt' the word 'genügt' is underlined. In '2, ... zur Erklärung nothwendig ist' the word 'nothwendig' is underlined. The machine transcription does not mark this emphasis.
The pencil number '10' in the right margin is the folio number. It is not part of the text.
